title_ar: الشيخ الددو يشارك في مؤتمر الإغاثة الدولي لصالح الشعب السوري في العاصمة اسطنبول
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the International Relief Conference for the Syrian People in Istanbul
body_ar:
يشارك الشيخ العلامة محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين في المؤتمر الإغاثي الدولي المنظم في العاصمة التركية اسطنبول لصالح الشعب السوري من طرف جمعية الأيادي البيضاء تحت عنوان رحماء بينهم في الفترة من 18 إلي 20 فبراير الجاري ويضم المؤتمر عددا كبيرا من العاملين في المجال الخيري والمهتمين بقضية الشعب السوري الذي يعاني ويلات الحرب بسبب النظام الجائر الذي يفرض نفسه قسرا على الشعب وينكل به أشد تنكيل.

وقد افتتح الشيخ ورشات اليوم الأول بكلمة بين فيها وجوب دعم الشعب السوري في محنته من عدة أوجه ليس أقلها أهمية رد الجميل لبلد أخرج في جميع عصور الدولة الإسلامية علماء أفذاذ واستقبل طلاب العلم من جميع أقطار العالم، ونهل من معين علمه وحضارته عطاش فنون العلم والحضارة.

وختم الشيخ الددو كلمته بشكر كل الأيادي البيضاء التي اجمعت من مختلف الدول لتقديم العون والمساعدة للشعب السوري، كما شكر الدولة المستضيفة على استضافتها لهذا المؤتمر وعلى كل ما تقدمه للقضية السورية.

كما أدار الشيخ ورشة حول موضوع سنة التمكين شارك فيها أساتذة ومشايخ ومهتمون بالعمل الخيري والإنساني

واليوم سيلقي الشيخ محاضرة عن الأحكام المتعلقة بإدارة أموال التبرعات والزكاة.

وخارج برنامج المؤتمر استضافت الشيخ جمعية الحكمة للعلم والصداقة والتعاون حيث ألقى بها محاضرة حول واقع الأمة حضرها جمع ضم عددا من الطلاب الموريتانيين المقيمين في اسطنبول، وفي نهاية المحاضرة قدم اتحاد الطلاب درعا للشيخ تكريما له على جهوده العلمية في خدمة القضايا المشتركة والمصيرية للأمة الإسلامية.
body_en:
The learned Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars and president of the Abdullah ibn Yasin University, is taking part in the international relief conference organised in the Turkish capital, Istanbul, for the benefit of the Syrian people, by the White Hands Association, under the title "Merciful Among Themselves", in the period from 18 to 20 February this year. The conference brings together a large number of those working in the charitable field and those concerned with the cause of the Syrian people, who are suffering the calamities of war because of the oppressive regime that imposes itself upon the people by force and inflicts the harshest abuse upon them.

The Sheikh opened the first day's workshops with an address in which he set out the obligation (wujūb) of supporting the Syrian people in their ordeal on several grounds, not the least important of which is the repayment of a debt of gratitude to a land which, in every age of the Islamic state, brought forth peerless scholars and received students of knowledge from every quarter of the world, and from the spring of whose learning and civilisation those thirsting for the arts of learning and of civilisation have drunk.

Sheikh al-Dedew closed his address by thanking all the white hands that had gathered from various countries to offer aid and assistance to the Syrian people; and he thanked the host state for its hosting of this conference and for all that it offers to the Syrian cause.

The Sheikh also chaired a workshop on the subject of the divine pattern of establishment in the land (sunnat al-tamkīn), in which teachers, sheikhs and people concerned with charitable and humanitarian work took part.

Today the Sheikh will deliver a lecture on the rulings relating to the administration of donated funds and of zakat.

Outside the conference programme, the Sheikh was hosted by the Wisdom Association for Knowledge, Friendship and Co-operation, where he delivered a lecture on the condition of the Ummah, attended by a gathering that included a number of Mauritanian students resident in Istanbul. At the end of the lecture, the students' union presented the Sheikh with a shield in tribute to his scholarly efforts in the service of the shared and decisive causes of the Islamic Ummah.

flags.arabic: صيغة الخبر الصحفي (قال فضيلة الشيخ... مؤكدا... وأضاف...)
options: render as a site news report, with the Sheikh's words marked as the site's paraphrase
render as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: NOT A TEXT BY THE SHEIKH. This record is the site's own news write-up. Outside the passages placed in quotation marks, every formulation is the site editor's indirect report of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and the English preserves the reporting verbs (the Sheikh said that..., he affirmed that...) so that a reader can see this. It must not be displayed as a fatwa or as a text of his. The underlying address or lecture is not in this record.

flags.arabic: بكلمة بين فيها وجوب دعم الشعب السوري في محنته
flags.context: the summary of the Sheikh's opening address at the relief conference
options: the obligation (wujūb) of supporting the Syrian people
that supporting the Syrian people is obligatory (wājib)
the necessity of supporting the Syrian people
flags.note: EDITORIAL and RULING-WORD. وجوب is the verbal noun of wājib, so the five-rulings mapping applies and 'obligation' is correct; 'necessity' would weaken it and is not used. But the ruling is the REPORTER'S summary of an address, not a fatwa the Sheikh wrote, and what is described throughout the record is humanitarian relief — donations, aid, the administration of charitable funds and zakat. Solicitation of funds for Syria is a regulated and, in several Western jurisdictions, a criminally sensitive area, and an English page that reads as a scholar declaring it obligatory to fund a Syrian cause can be received very differently from the Arabic. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened; whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the subject of the workshop the Sheikh chaired
options: the divine pattern of establishment in the land (sunnat al-tamkīn)
the way in which God grants ascendancy
flags.note: Not in the glossary; a candidate for addition. Here sunnah is NOT the prophetic sunnah of the glossary but a sunnah kawniyyah, a recurring pattern God has set in history, so the English must not read as 'the Prophet's sunnah of empowerment'. tamkīn is the Qur'anic 'establishing in the land' (e.g. 24:55). 'Empowerment' is a false friend with modern political overtones and has been avoided. The workshop's content is not in the record.

flags.arabic: النظام الجائر الذي يفرض نفسه قسرا على الشعب وينكل به أشد تنكيل
flags.context: the site's description of the Syrian government
options: translate the site's characterisation as the site's own, in reported form
attribute the characterisation to Sheikh al-Dedew
flags.note: ATTRIBUTION. This description of the Syrian government is the SITE EDITOR's framing in the opening sentence, not a quotation from the Sheikh, who is not reported as saying it. The English keeps it inside the reporter's sentence. It must not be presented as his statement about a head of state.

The title is a phrase of the Qur'an (Sūrat al-Fatḥ 48:29). The source prints it without quotation marks or a reference; quotation marks have been added in the English only to mark it as a title, and no Qur'anic citation has been added, since the source gives none. Style guide section 4 note: Qur'anic renderings are interpretive.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: إلي in 'من 18 إلي 20' is the source's spelling of إلى; preserved in body_ar.
اجمعت ('gathered') is the source's spelling for اجتمعت; translated by the evident sense.
جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين is the Abdullah ibn Yasin University in Nouakchott; the name is kept in standard romanisation without diacritics per style guide section 2.
The 'white hands' of the closing paragraph is a play on the name of the organising association (al-Ayadi al-Bayda, the White Hands); kept literal so the play survives.
